labels.label: btzthm:BTZ_ext
labels.notes: GX.BTZMax.btz_ext_of_countableLines (RichardsSplit.lean:88) has the conclusion of GX.BTZMax.btz_ext (MaxExtension.lean:522) token for token: IsMaximal, IsInextensible, universal, every maximal one Equivalent. The instance binders are the same. The only change is the input: hR : RichardsInput M becomes hL : CountableLinesInput M, and the proof is btz_ext hG (richardsInput_of_countableLines hL). CountableLinesInput (LineStructure.lean:641) has RichardsInput's setting and concludes that the set of components of S0 C is countable. That matches l.1544's « sing₀(M̄) has at most countably many connected components ». It is equivalent to RichardsInput (richardsInput_iff_countableLines, LineStructure.lean:657), so this is the same strength. Lean < paper is fully disclosed in the checklist and SCOPE, and the row stays partial: E0 only (T-btz-scope), M connected added, named cited input (OQ-150 (c)). Unmarked. chainsInherit_of_countableLines is chainsInherit on the narrowed input. The claim that universality and uniqueness use no cited input checks out: isUniversal_of_isMaximal (MaxExtension.lean:491) and equivalent_of_isMaximal (l.505) take no RichardsInput.

labels.label: btzthm:maximal_btz_extension
labels.notes: BTZ_1.tex l.1269-1271 states the same theorem, with « unique up to isomorphism ». Equivalence over M is at least as strong. The same disclosures apply, and the row stays partial and unmarked. The proposed blocked_on, which replaces GX.BTZMax.RichardsInput with GX.BTZLine.CountableLinesInput, names the iff and btz_ext_of_countableLines, and keeps T-btz-scope and OQ-150, is accurate. Both T-btz-scope (roadmap) and OQ-150 (DECISIONS.md:378, OPEN) exist.
